# All

Tells whether a lambda gives a truthy result for every element of an array.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
All(items, callback)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | array | The array to test. Null is read as the empty array; any other type that is not an array is a runtime error. |
| `callback` | function | A lambda of exactly one parameter, which receives the element; its result is tested for being truthy. A lambda of any other number of parameters, or a value that is not a lambda, null included, is a runtime error. |

## Returns

Boolean. True when the lambda's result is truthy for every element, and so true for an empty array; false otherwise. Never null.

## Remarks

The lambda is called for each element in order, and not for any element after the first one that gives a result that is not truthy. It is given the elements the array holds when the call starts, so a change the lambda makes to the array does not change which elements it is given.

## Example

`All([2, 4, 6], x => x % 2 == 0)` returns true.
